about.title: Saving tips
about.typical: A device of this kind usually draws {typical} W when on; yours averages {yours} W.

tips.ac: Set it to 26 °C or higher; each degree lower adds roughly 6 to 8 percent to its energy use.
tips.fridge: Keep door seals clean and the fridge away from heat; a full fridge runs more efficiently.
tips.freezer: Defrost regularly and keep it full; ice build-up makes the compressor work harder.
tips.fridge_freezer: Leave a gap behind the unit for airflow and do not set the temperature colder than needed.
tips.washing_machine: Wash full loads in cold water when possible; heating the water is most of the energy.
tips.washer_dryer: Drying uses far more energy than washing; air-dry when the weather allows.
tips.tumble_dryer: Clean the lint filter every load and spin clothes well before drying.
tips.dishwasher: Run only full loads and use the eco programme to cut heating energy.
tips.television: Lower the screen brightness and switch the TV off rather than leaving it on standby.
tips.computer: Enable sleep mode and switch off the power strip when you are away for long.
tips.microwave: Microwaves are efficient for small portions; avoid using the oven to reheat them.
tips.kettle: Boil only the water you need; it is a short but high-power appliance.
tips.toaster: Short, high-power bursts; unplug it when not in use.
tips.hifi: Amplifiers draw power even when idle; turn them off at the switch.
tips.electric_heater: Heat the room you are in, not the whole house, and use a thermostat or timer.
tips.router: Always on but low power; consider switching it off overnight if nothing needs it.
tips.water_heater: Lower the thermostat and switch it off when no one needs hot water.
tips.electric_car: Charge outside peak hours and set a charge limit to avoid wasted energy.
tips.lights: Switch to LED bulbs and turn lights off in empty rooms.
tips.oven: Avoid opening the door while cooking and use the residual heat at the end.

tips.alwaysOn: Background load is what the home draws when nobody is using anything: router, chargers, devices on standby. Every 10 W running all year costs about 88 kWh.
tips.fridge: Keep it 10 cm from the wall, keep the door seals clean and set the fridge to 3–5 °C. Longer runs than usual often mean a leaking seal or a dusty condenser.
tips.kettle: Boil only the water you need: a full kettle takes twice the time and energy of half a kettle.
tips.washer: Wash full loads in cold water; most of a washing machine's energy heats the water.
tips.tv: Lower the screen brightness and switch it off when nobody watches: standby still draws power.
tips.hifi: Amplifiers draw power even when idle; switch them off at the socket.
tips.dishwasher: Run only full loads on the eco programme, and skip heated drying when you can.
tips.microwave: For small portions a microwave uses less energy than the hob or the oven.
tips.toaster: High power in short bursts; unplug it when not in use.
tips.ac: Set it to 26 °C or higher; each degree lower adds about 6 to 8 percent to its energy use.
tips.waterHeater: Lower the thermostat and switch it off when no one needs hot water.
tips.riceCooker: Cook only what you need and unplug it once the rice is done instead of keeping it warm.
tips.other: Energy not yet put down to a device. It shrinks as the system learns more of the home's devices.
